record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
record.original_question: For languages recognized by k-edge deterministic finite-state automata over ranked alphabets, can one develop the usual formal-language theory: in particular, is there an appropriate pumping lemma, and what are the closure properties of these language classes under standard language operations?

evidence.quote: Clearly any k-edge Dfa is also a Dfa but the converse is not true. Moreover some regular languages cannot be represented by k-edge Dfa, for any k.
There are some accessory problems more in the line of general formal language theory: do we have a pumping lemma? what are the closure properties?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider deterministic finite-state automata over a ranked alphabet (an alphabet in which each symbol is assigned a fixed nonnegative integer arity). For a fixed positive integer k, define a k-edge deterministic finite-state automaton (k-edge DFA) to be a DFA in which the total number of transition edges is at most k. Let L_k denote the class of languages recognized by k-edge DFAs.

Every k-edge DFA is a DFA, so each language in L_k is regular; however, there exist regular languages that are not in L_k for any k. Develop the formal-language theory of the classes L_k. In particular:

(a) Establish a pumping lemma characterizing membership (or providing a necessary condition for membership) in L_k: find a structural property P(k) of words in L such that every sufficiently long word w in L admits a decomposition w = xyz (with y nonempty and obeying length constraints depending on k) for which xy^i z ∈ L for all i ≥ 0, in a form that meaningfully exploits the bound k on the number of edges.

(b) Determine the closure properties of L_k (and of the union ⋃_k L_k) under the standard language operations: union, intersection, concatenation, Kleene star, complement, homomorphism, inverse homomorphism, and intersection with regular languages. For each operation, decide whether the class is closed; when not closed, quantify how the parameter k must grow.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface published results establishing a pumping lemma or a systematic study of closure properties specifically for the class of languages recognized by k-edge deterministic finite-state automata over ranked alphabets. Standard sources address the classical regular-language pumping lemma and closure properties but not this restricted size-bounded variant. The current status of the problem could not be verified from accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: The Pumping Lemma and Closure Properties (lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard exposition of the pumping lemma and closure properties for regular languages; no treatment of k-edge DFAs.
status_evidence.claim: Available references discuss only the classical regular case, not the k-edge restricted class.
